Denial of Service through Email Flooding [Denial of Service, CWE-400] on aws-ses, aws-sqs-EmailQueue, aws-lambda-EmailProcessor, aws-elasticbeanstalk-AdminPanel: Attackers can send a large volume of emails or API requests without any throttling mechanisms in place. This could overwhelm system resources and impact service availability. An attacker writes a script to continuously send emails through the system, depleting SES quotas and overwhelming the email processing pipeline.

Insufficient Authentication and Authorization [Spoofing, Elevation of Privilege, CWE-287] on aws-elasticbeanstalk-AdminPanel, aws-lambda-NotificationManager, aws-ses: The system lacks proper authentication mechanisms, particularly for the admin panel and email services. No MFA requirement increases the risk of unauthorized access. An attacker gains access to the admin panel through weak credentials, allowing them to modify email configurations and access sensitive data.

Malware Distribution through Email Attachments [Tampering, Information Disclosure, CWE-434] on aws-s3-EmailArchiveBucket, aws-lambda-EmailProcessor, aws-ses: Malicious files can be attached to emails without proper scanning, potentially delivering malware to recipients or storing dangerous content in S3. An attacker sends an email with a malicious attachment that contains ransomware, which gets delivered to recipients without detection.

Insecure Data Storage and Access Controls [Information Disclosure, Elevation of Privilege, CWE-284] on aws-s3-EmailArchiveBucket, aws-dynamodb-MetricsStore, aws-lambda-EmailProcessor: Lack of proper access controls and encryption for stored emails could allow unauthorized access to sensitive data. An attacker exploits weak S3 bucket policies or IAM roles to access emails belonging to other users.

DNS Hijacking and Spoofing [Spoofing, Tampering, CWE-350] on aws-route53, aws-ses, aws-acm: Insufficient DNS security and lack of TLS could allow attackers to intercept or redirect email traffic. An attacker performs a DNS hijacking attack to redirect email traffic to their servers, capturing sensitive communications.

Spam and Phishing Distribution [Spoofing, Tampering, CWE-940] on aws-ses, aws-lambda-EmailProcessor: Without proper spam detection and content filtering, the system could be exploited to send malicious or unwanted emails. An attacker compromises the system to send phishing emails to recipients, potentially damaging the domain's reputation.

Insufficient Disaster Recovery and Backup [Information Disclosure, Denial of Service, CWE-912] on aws-s3-EmailArchiveBucket, aws-dynamodb-MetricsStore, aws-elasticbeanstalk-AdminPanel: Without proper backup and recovery procedures, system failures or attacks could result in permanent data loss. A ransomware attack encrypts critical data, and the lack of proper backups prevents service restoration.
